2607.28628.title: Learning to Trace Seiberg Dualities
2607.28628.paper_summary: Dualities play an important role in establishing both microscopic and emergent phenomena in a wide range of physical systems. In practice, though, it can often be computationally challenging to establish when two systems are dual, even when all of the "rules of the game" are well-known. Said differently, when confronted with two systems, how can one efficiently establish that they are in fact dual? In this paper we use machine learning methods to address this question for Seiberg dualities of supersymmetric quiver gauge theories. Mathematically, this involves establishing mutations of quivers, which is in turn a variation on the theme of "learning to unknot". On the one hand, this leads us to a practical tool for establishing the computational complexity of different dualities. On the other hand, it also allows us to study how different network architectures learn how to trace Seiberg dualities. We find that for quivers with a modest number of quiver nodes (of order $10$), different network architectures consisting of transformers and multi-layer perceptrons tend to outperform deterministic algorithms. Supplementing the network by well-established pathfinder algorithms (essentially "Google Maps for quivers") leads to an additional improvement in the efficiency and accuracy of the search strategy. We anticipate that this class of questions can serve as a useful benchmark for frontier AI models applied to theoretical physics.
2607.28628.paper_summary_zh: 雙重性在建立微觀和突現現象的各種物理系統中扮演著重要角色。<lb/>然而，在實踐中，儘管所有的「遊戲規則」都已知，確定兩個系統是否為雙重性仍然常常在計算上具有挑戰性。<lb/>換句話說，面對兩個系統時，如何有效地確定它們實際上是雙重的？<lb/>在本文中，我們使用機器學習方法來解決這個問題，針對超對稱箭形規範理論的Seiberg雙重性進行探討。<lb/>在數學上，這涉及到確定箭形的變異，這反過來又是「學習解開結」這一主題的一種變體。<lb/>一方面，這使我們能夠獲得一種實用工具，用於確定不同雙重性的計算複雜性。<lb/>另一方面，它還使我們能夠研究不同的網絡架構如何學習追蹤Seiberg雙重性。<lb/>我們發現，對於具有適度數量箭形節點（約為$10$）的箭形，不同的網絡架構，包括Transformer和多層感知器，往往表現優於確定性算法。<lb/>通過成熟的路徑尋找算法（本質上是「箭形的谷歌地圖」）來補充網絡，進一步提高了搜尋策略的效率和準確性。<lb/>我們預期這類問題可以作為應用於理論物理的前沿AI模型的一個有用基準。
